evals.prompt: Our Q3 NPS came back at 34, down from 41. Here's the export. What do I tell the exec team on Thursday?
evals.expected_output: A readout that leads with representativeness before the score, ranks themes by ARR rather than mention count, and asks its scoping questions in one batched tappable ask.
assertions: Asks scope, period, capacity-to-act and output audience as a single batched AskUserQuestion of no more than four, each with 2-4 options and the recommended one first and labelled '(Recommended)'
Never states the 34 or the 41 without the response rate, respondent count and ARR represented in the same place
Prints §1 representativeness, including a Silent ARR table by segment with renewals inside 120 days, before any theme ranking
Ranks themes by attributed ARR x severity x trajectory x tractability, never by mention count, and shows the arithmetic
Labels the attributed-ARR column as revenue of accounts that mentioned the theme, not revenue at risk or recoverable
Ends with a Coverage Ledger over all seven signal families and a confidence capped by coverage
Names no CS-platform vendor product anywhere; refers to the category generically ("your CS platform", "whichever platform holds your playbooks")

evals.prompt: Here's a dump of 400 support tickets and 60 survey verbatims from the last two quarters. Pull out the themes and tell me which ones to take to Product.
evals.expected_output: Coded themes against a versioned taxonomy with an inter-coder alpha, ARR attached per theme, one accountable owner each, and everything below the capacity cut written into a Not Doing section.
assertions: Runs ../cs-context/scripts/ingest.py on the supplied files before quoting any number from them
Confirms every column mapping below 0.80 confidence before using those numbers, and asks for the export's as-of date
Codes the problem rather than the requested solution, and states one primary code per mention
Reports an inter-coder alpha with its sample size and coder types, and states that an LLM coder is held to the same double-coding audit
Assigns exactly one accountable owner per routed theme with an action, a date, an expected effect and a success measure
Puts every theme below the capacity-gate cut into a 'Not Doing' section with a reason and a reconsider trigger
Records any default it proceeded on in an Assumptions table with a concrete 'if wrong' consequence, not 'may affect results'

evals.prompt: Draft the follow-up to the three detractors from this quarter's survey, and the you-said-we-did note that goes out to everyone.
evals.expected_output: Internal analysis above an unmissable divider, then each customer-facing draft inside its own fenced text block, formatted for an email client and free of internal language.
assertions: Every customer-facing draft sits inside a fenced ```text block below the CUSTOMER-FACING divider, with the internal analysis above it
The fenced blocks contain no unfilled placeholders such as [Name] or [Date]; any genuinely unavailable value is raised above the divider as 'UNKNOWN — requires X'
No health score, risk band, ARR figure, forecast category, save play, coverage tier or internal theme code appears inside any fence
Blocks are formatted for an email client: plain text with blank lines between paragraphs and bullet characters, no markdown headings, no pipe tables, no ** bold
None of 'just checking in', 'touching base', 'circling back', 'hope you're well', 'reaching out', 'we value your partnership' or 'let me know your thoughts' appears in any draft
The outer-loop note includes a 'what we are not doing, and why' section and is addressed to non-respondents as well as respondents
The promoter path makes an advocacy ask only, with no expansion ask in the same conversation

evals.prompt: We only have NPS from about 12% of accounts and no call transcripts. Is it even worth doing a VoC readout this quarter?
evals.expected_output: A direct answer with the coverage arithmetic, a partial artifact rather than a refusal, and an explicit capacity-to-act recommendation.
assertions: Computes sentiment ARR coverage as ARR of accounts with feedback divided by in-scope ARR, and states the figure
Says plainly that below roughly 50% ARR coverage the sentiment section is anecdote rather than measurement, and caps confidence accordingly
Produces a partial artifact with a coverage figure rather than refusing, stopping only below 40% coverage
Names the missing signal families in a Coverage Ledger and says what those gaps typically hide
Runs the capacity-to-act gate and recommends against collecting more survey data if nobody can act on it
Gives a decisive recommendation rather than a menu of options, with an owner and a date
